items.title: Invited talk on polyspectral mean estimation at IISA 2026
items.summary: I will present invited work on polyspectral mean estimation for general nonlinear processes at the International Indian Statistical Association conference. The work develops higher-order spectral tools for inference on nonlinear and non-Gaussian time series.

items.title: Faruk Muritala receives student grant and presents research at SEASUG 2026
items.summary: Doctoral researcher Faruk Muritala attended SEASUG 2026 as a student grant recipient and presented ongoing research on smoking during pregnancy and preterm birth. He also moderated a session on building Excel reports from SAS, contributing both as a presenter and session moderator.

items.title: Two LINDT-C projects selected as ARISE 2026 finalists
items.summary: Two projects involving the LINDT-C Lab were selected as finalists for the ASA Statistics and Data Science in Aging Interest Group's ARISE 2026 Webinar Series. The selections include work led with Imaan Shahid and a second project with Sheng Luo, with each finalist invited to present in the 2026 webinar series.

items.title: Student-led fake-news paper accepted for publication in AJUR
items.summary: Our student-led work on distinguishing AI-generated and human-written fake news has been accepted for publication in the American Journal of Undergraduate Research. The project grew from undergraduate research with Samuel Jaeger, Calvin Ibenye, and Aya Vera-Jimenez.

items.title: Georgia overdose mortality study accepted in Spatial and Spatio-temporal Epidemiology
items.summary: The study "Spatiotemporal Characterization of Overdose Mortality in Georgia, USA Using Spectral and Nonlinear Interaction Analysis, 2003–2021" has been accepted for publication in Spatial and Spatio-temporal Epidemiology. The paper combines spatial, spectral, and nonlinear interaction analysis to characterize changing overdose mortality patterns across Georgia.

items.title: Spatial health analytics paper accepted as a full paper at HCist 2026
items.summary: Work with Samhita Pal and Dilshad Imon, “Temporally Resolved Spatial Health Analytics for Environmental Exposure Surveillance: PM2.5, COPD, and Stroke across U.S. Cities,” has been accepted for presentation at HCist 2026 and for inclusion in the conference proceedings as a full paper. The study links historical PM2.5 exposure with later COPD and stroke prevalence trends across 70 U.S. cities using geographically weighted regression.

items.title: First-Year Scholars misinformation project accepted at ICMLA 2026
items.summary: Work with undergraduate researchers Calvin Ibenye, Aya-Vera Jimenez, and Samuel Jaeger examines why AI-generated and human-written misinformation differ in detectability. The project grew from Kennesaw State's First-Year Scholars program and will be presented at ICMLA 2026.

items.title: ivgls released on CRAN
items.summary: The ivgls R package is now available on CRAN. Developed with Samhita Pal, the package implements network-aware instrumental-variable regression with graph-fused regularization, including procedures designed to accommodate invalid instruments.

items.title: Imaan Shahid wins second place at KSU C-Day
items.summary: Imaan Shahid, then an M.S. student in Data Science and Analytics and now a doctoral researcher in the LINDT-C Lab, won second place at Kennesaw State University's C-Day research showcase. The recognition highlights her student research within the lab's longitudinal and statistical methodology program.

items.title: Master's research on causal GNNs for Alzheimer's disease featured at KSU C-Day
items.summary: Pranay Kumar Peddi presented our Causal-GCN project, which combines graph neural networks with causal adjustment to study model-based influence of brain regions in Alzheimer's disease. The work uses ADNI imaging data and later appeared in the DATA 2026 proceedings.

items.title: Review of statistical and machine-learning approaches to clinical-trial efficacy published
items.summary: A review with Samhita Pal surveys classical, nonparametric, Bayesian, and machine-learning approaches to efficacy analysis in clinical trials, with attention to longitudinal outcomes, missing data, complex endpoint structures, and modern predictive methods.

items.title: Demographic distribution matching study published in Medical Physics
items.summary: Our Duke collaboration introduces DISTINCT, a distributional subsampling framework for aligning real-world and virtual phantom populations. The study connects statistical distribution matching with virtual imaging-trial design and lung-cancer screening applications.

items.title: Bot-detection paper published in IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
items.summary: This interdisciplinary collaboration with William Boettcher and Rob Johnston combines temporal and semantic features from social-media behavior with machine learning and conformal prediction for uncertainty-aware bot detection.
